newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks set record close, turnover.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks set record close, turnover.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks thundered to a record close on Friday, powered by a scramble for the market's bluest blue chips and interest in a surprising red-chip deal, brokers said.
The index gained 190.5 points, or 1.39 percent, to end at a record closing high of 13,930.80. The previous record close was 13,868.24, set on January 20.
Turnover swelled to HK$17.85 billion, the single heaviest day in the exchange's history.
On Thursday, turnover was a hefty HK$14.04 billion.
The index also set a new all-time high of 14,047.20 on Friday.

"The record highs on Wall Street have given us the room to move ahead today," said Francis Wong, executive director at DBS Securities. "But the bulk of the short-term movement is due to derivative and hedge fund players."

The market gapped up just after the start of trade with a leap in HSBC Holdings. The share hit a record high of HK$219.00 before easing to close at HK$217.00, a gain of HK$7.00 on very heavy turnover of HK$1.58 billion.

The rise in HSBC was fuelled partly by shortcovering, a continuation of the scramble for the bank's shares seen in London overnight and due to its usefulness as a hedge against index futures, brokers said.
"There could be a fundamental reason, the perennial speculation that the bank will restructure its Hong Kong operations," said one banking analyst with a Japanese house.
"But the share is reaching its 1997 year-end target of HK$220 to HK$240."
May Hang Seng Index futures, which traded at a premium to the market for most of the day, closed at a discount.
The May contract closed 230 points higher at 13,915.
"The market turned volatile in the afternoon," said Kenneth Tang, director at Sassoon Futures.

The focus in the afternoon session turned to Hong Kong Telecommunications and CITIC Pacific, which resumed trading after being suspended in the morning. CITIC Pacific announced it was selling its 7.74 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom to Beijing-based China Everbright Holdings.
CITIC Pacific hit a high of HK$45.40 then slipped to end HK$0.90 higher at HK$44.40. Hongkong Telecom shot to a high of HK$15.90 but ended HK$0.50 lower at HK$14.50.
